## 2. Statement of Facts

Dr. Rhea Malhotra, a medical professional providing telemedicine consultancy services, earned gross receipts of INR 42 lakh for the relevant financial year, of which more than 95% was received through banking or other digital modes.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether Dr. Malhotra is eligible to opt for presumptive taxation under Section 44ADA, having regard to the enhanced turnover threshold introduced by the Finance Act, 2023.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 44ADA
- Section 44AA
- Section 44AB


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- Not applicable / no specific provisions beyond the Income-tax Act general scheme.

## 6. Analysis

The Finance Act, 2023 enhanced the Section 44ADA threshold from INR 50 lakh to INR 75 lakh, subject to the condition that cash receipts do not exceed 5% of total gross receipts. Dr. Malhotra's receipts of INR 42 lakh are within even the original threshold, and comfortably within the enhanced threshold given that over 95% of receipts are digital.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

Dr. Malhotra is eligible to opt for presumptive taxation under Section 44ADA and may offer 50% of gross receipts (INR 21 lakh) as deemed professional income, without the requirement to maintain detailed books of account or undergo a tax audit.
